 NBA Investigation Rumor Surrounds Sabonis After Scoreless Game
 Nov 19, 2026 • 12:34 
 • 7 Reads 
 Wulan Hapsari 
 Share 
 Imago IMAGO / ZUMA Press Wire 
 Font Size 
 A− 
 A 
 A+ 
 Bsinews.id, Jakarta , Uncertainty surrounding Domantas Sabonis has intensified as the Sacramento Kings struggle through a difficult NBA season, following an unusual scoreless performance against the Orlando Magic. Reports circulating on social media have suggested that the league is examining the center's conduct, but no official announcement or credible reporting has confirmed an investigation.
 According to BasketballNews, the speculation emerged after Sabonis recorded zero points in 24 minutes against Orlando on Tuesday. He attempted just two field goals, including one three-pointer, missed both attempts and also failed to convert two free throws. He nevertheless contributed two rebounds and five assists.

 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 The available reporting offers no verified evidence of an investigation involving Sabonis. The NBA has made no public statement concerning the player, while established coverage has focused primarily on questions surrounding his effort and future in Sacramento.

 Darius Acuff Joins Jordan and Robertson in Elite Rookie Club 
 Basketball analyst Kevin O'Connor described Sabonis as someone who "doesn't want to be there." The phrase "quiet quitting" subsequently became associated with discussions about the player's situation, although those comments did not establish any official league inquiry.
 Sabonis has also faced uncertainty over his position in Sacramento amid persistent trade discussions. He previously told NBC Sports Bay Area that he was "shocked" to see his name included in offseason trade reports.
 The Kings' difficult campaign provides additional context. Sacramento had fallen to 1-12 by November 18, according to BasketballNews, following another disappointing stretch of results. The team has also considered potential roster changes, with The Athletic's Sam Amick reporting that the organization was willing to entertain offers for almost every player except rookie Darius Acuff Jr.
 Also Read 
 Suns Face Kings as Darius Acuff Jr. Leads Sacramento 
 Sabonis' financial commitments could complicate a potential departure. His contract is worth $45.4 million this season and $48.6 million next season, making a suitable trade arrangement more challenging.
 Physical condition and changing responsibilities also offer possible explanations for his reduced production. Sabonis is recovering from an injury and surgery that sidelined him for most of the previous season. He also reportedly missed the game immediately before facing Orlando because of related ankle problems, despite saying he was fully recovered.
 His offensive responsibilities have also shifted as Sacramento increasingly distributes scoring opportunities among Acuff and Zach LaVine. His five assists against Orlando reflected a performance in which he contributed more through playmaking than shooting.
 Also Read 
 Wembanyama Limits Dunks After Developing Painful Blister 
 That difficult outing was followed by a substantial improvement against Portland on November 13. According to NBC Sports Bay Area, Sabonis recorded 21 points, 12 rebounds and five assists in the Kings' 120-107 defeat to the Trail Blazers, earning his eighth double-double of the season.
 His opening-quarter performance against Portland included eight points, six rebounds and three assists. He also produced a dunk through defensive traffic and connected from three-point range during the fourth quarter.
 Portland secured the victory through strong performances from Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard, who scored 34 and 29 points respectively. Their contributions extended Sacramento's losing streak to five games and left the Kings with a 1-11 record at that stage.
 Also Read 
 Olivier-Maxence Prosper Scores Five Points in Grizzlies Win 
 Meanwhile, head coach Doug Christie praised the return of forward Keegan Murray, who rejoined the starting lineup after missing seven games because of left ankle capsulitis. Murray finished with a season-high 16 points, seven rebounds and four assists.
 Christie highlighted Murray's personality and approach to the game, describing him as dependable despite his injury setbacks.
 "Keegan's a little bit stoic," Kings coach Doug Christie said.
 Also Read 
 Blazers Weigh Scoot Henderson Trade After Continued Struggles 
 Christie also emphasized the importance of restoring the forward's confidence and enjoyment on the court.
 "You know he's just going to be a fantastic warrior for you through whatever it is. But for him, what I want is, I want joy. I want him to go out and have fun and play free.
 We've seen it a couple of times, we've seen it in flashes. But he deserves that. He's a great kid, he works extremely hard."
 Also Read 
 Antetokounmpo Leads Heat Past Bucks in Miami Debut 
 The coach acknowledged that injuries could create doubts for players returning to competition, but expressed confidence in Murray's ability to regain his previous form.
 "... I know that sometimes it's difficult when you start to get injuries and different things. Sometimes you question yourself a little bit, but he doesn't need to question himself.
 He's a damn good player. We value him very highly and he'll see his way through it. It's just those things unfortunately take time, but having him back in uniform is, like I told you guys previously, it makes me smile because I like to see him out there."
 Acuff also experienced an uneven night against Portland before finishing strongly. The rookie scored 17 points, including 10 in the fourth quarter, but shot just 6 of 19 from the field. His playing time was limited to 23 minutes through the first three quarters as Christie continued managing his workload after the rookie had led the NBA in minutes played.
 For Sabonis, the Portland performance demonstrated a significant statistical rebound from his scoreless appearance against Orlando. However, the claims surrounding an NBA investigation remained unverified as of November 18, with no official league confirmation.
